newsitem.title: USA: NHL ice hockey-ROOKIES TAKE IT FROM THE VETERANS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ice hockey-ROOKIES TAKE IT FROM THE VETERANS.

text.p: The Philadelphia Flyers entered Game One of the NHL Eastern Conference finals considerably younger and far bigger, but were missing key seasoning at deep post season play.

Their opponents, the New York Rangers, on the other hand, were touted as a team peaking at just the right time behind the veterans of several Stanley Cup champion teams and a goaltender at the top of his game.

With Mike Richter stopping 96 percent of the pucks shot at him in the first two rounds of the playoffs and the knowledge that only names like former Edmonton Oilers Wayne Gretzky, Mark Messier, Esa Tikkanen bring to the postseason, the Flyers were expected to need all their wits to match them against the sages of the NHL.
But the Flyers rode the backs of their rookies to a 3-1 victory in the first game.

With less than five minutes played in the first period, 18-year-old Dainius Zubrus and 21-year-old Janne Niinimaa had pumped two quick goals behind Richter and the Flyers were secure enough to settle into a tightly-played defensive game.
Their two ages combined barely exceed that of either the Rangers captain, Messier, or teammate Gretzky, both 36.

Flyers head coach Terry Murray realises that flash and speed will be a great asset against a Ranger team that has been tagged as the over-the-hill gang. That is precisely why Zubrus got the call to play on the Flyers top line alongside superstars Eric Lindros and John LeClair.

"Zubrus is 6-foot-3 (1.9 meters), 220 pounds (99.7 kg), 18 years old. He's playing on the line that he's on tonight and certainly not looking out of place," Murray said after the game. "With what he's got ahead of him, it's going to be a little bit scary - what kind of a player he's going to be."

Following Zubrus's first goal of the game was Niinimaa's, a blast from the point that came with a man advantage after Alexander Karpovtsev was penalised for tripping at 3:06 in the first period. Niinimaa was wide open and not even the craftiest Ranger was capable of finding a way to stop the goal.
"For Niinimaa not to be one of the three finalists (for rookie of the year) this year is absolutely beyond comprehension," Murray said.
"A couple of years ago we didn't have the depth, we didn't have any young guys coming into the organisation who could step in and play. Throughout the playoffs they've contributed."
